Copy any code you want to keep before leaving or reloading the page.

study_accession = readStudyAccession(window.location.search)

## Set up

The study accession comes from the box above. To use this code in local Python,
set `STUDY` to an accession such as `"MGYS00010393"`.

```{pyodide}
#| input: [study_accession]
from io import BytesIO
import requests
import pandas as pd

API = "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/metagenomics/api/v2"
STUDY = study_accession

def get_json(path, **params):
    response = requests.get(f"{API}/{path}", params=params, timeout=30)
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()

print(STUDY)
```

## Get a study

A study groups related samples and analyses. Retrieve its title and biome:

```{pyodide}
study = get_json(f"studies/{STUDY}")
print(study["title"])
study["biome"]
```

## List its analyses

List responses contain `items` and a total `count`. Fetch the first 20 analyses;
change `page=1` to `page=2` to get the next page.

```{pyodide}
batch = get_json(f"studies/{STUDY}/analyses/", page=1, page_size=20)
analyses = batch["items"]
print(f"Showing {len(analyses)} of {batch['count']} analyses")
pd.DataFrame(analyses).reindex(
    columns=["accession", "experiment_type", "pipeline_version"]
)
```

## Inspect an analysis

Choose the first analysis, or replace `ANALYSIS` with another accession from the
list. Its detail record includes the available result files.

```{pyodide}
if not analyses:
    raise ValueError("This study has no analyses. Choose another study above.")

ANALYSIS = analyses[0]["accession"]
analysis = get_json(f"analyses/{ANALYSIS}")
downloads = pd.DataFrame(analysis["downloads"])
downloads.reindex(columns=["short_description", "file_type", "alias"])
```

## Read a result table

For this analysis, load the Pfam domain-count summary into pandas. Other analyses
may have different files; use the descriptions above to choose a result.

```{pyodide}
matches = [d for d in analysis["downloads"]
           if d["short_description"] == "Pfam accession counts"]
if not matches:
    raise ValueError("No Pfam table for this analysis. Choose another analysis.")

response = requests.get(matches[0]["url"], timeout=30)
response.raise_for_status()
table = pd.read_csv(BytesIO(response.content), sep="\t", compression="gzip")
table.head()
```

The download is a gzip-compressed TSV. `compression="gzip"` decompresses it
before pandas reads the columns. Choose small summaries when working in your browser.

## Explore the counts

Show the ten most frequent Pfam domains. Try changing `10` to `20`.

```{pyodide}
table.sort_values("count", ascending=False).head(10)
```
